string-array.name: freedom_verses
string-array.item: Stone walls do not a prison make,\nNor iron bars a cage.\n— Richard Lovelace
I am the master of my fate,\nI am the captain of my soul.\n— W. E. Henley
Hope is the thing with feathers\nThat perches in the soul.\n— Emily Dickinson
I know why the caged bird sings.\n— Paul Laurence Dunbar
Give me liberty, or give me death!\n— Patrick Henry
Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.\n— Jean-Jacques Rousseau
The only freedom which deserves the name is that of pursuing our own good in our own way.\n— John Stuart Mill
Give me the liberty to know, to utter, and to argue freely according to conscience, above all liberties.\n— John Milton
Afoot and light-hearted I take to the open road,\nHealthy, free, the world before me.\n— Walt Whitman
I am large, I contain multitudes.\n— Walt Whitman
Resist much, obey little.\n— Walt Whitman
I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately.\n— Henry David Thoreau
If a man does not keep pace with his companions, perhaps it is because he hears a different drummer.\n— Henry David Thoreau
Whoso would be a man must be a nonconformist.\n— Ralph Waldo Emerson
Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.\n— Ralph Waldo Emerson
To be great is to be misunderstood.\n— Ralph Waldo Emerson
If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?\n— Percy Bysshe Shelley
Rise like Lions after slumber\nIn unvanquishable number!\n— Percy Bysshe Shelley
I must Create a System, or be enslav\'d by another Man\'s.\n— William Blake
Hereditary bondsmen! know ye not\nWho would be free themselves must strike the blow?\n— Lord Byron
Bliss was it in that dawn to be alive,\nBut to be young was very heaven!\n— William Wordsworth
I could be bounded in a nutshell, and count myself a king of infinite space.\n— William Shakespeare
Liberty! Freedom! Tyranny is dead!\n— William Shakespeare
Into that heaven of freedom, my Father,\nlet my country awake.\n— Rabindranath Tagore
Where the mind is without fear and the head is held high.\n— Rabindranath Tagore
He only earns his freedom and existence\nWho daily conquers them anew.\n— Goethe, trans. Bayard Taylor
Have courage to use your own understanding!\n— Immanuel Kant
Only the educated are free.\n— Epictetus
We are all slaves of the law in order that we may be free.\n— Cicero
The secret of happiness is freedom, and the secret of freedom is courage.\n— Thucydides
The world is my country, all mankind are my brethren, and to do good is my religion.\n— Thomas Paine
If there is no struggle, there is no progress.\n— Frederick Douglass
I do not wish them to have power over men; but over themselves.\n— Mary Wollstonecraft
We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.\n— Declaration of Independence
This nation, under God, shall have a new birth of freedom.\n— Abraham Lincoln
The caged bird longs for its old forest,\nthe pond fish pines for its native deep.\n— Tao Yuanming
The wren nests in the deep wood\nand needs no more than a single branch.\n— Zhuangzi
Why not whistle and stroll on?\nA lifetime of mist and rain, I take it as it comes.\n— Su Shi
Better to die than to have a mind that is not free.\n— Chen Yinque
